question_text: Read the following text and fill in each gap with a suitable word based on the information of the text.
stimulus: Unit−12; Lesson−2(D)  1  5 = 5 Many people go to cities and forget their roots knowingly or unknowingly. The specialty of that they are living to their village. Mr. Islam and his brothers are great as they haven't Islam is a graduate from Bangladesh Agricultural University in Mymenstngh. He advanced farming. His other two brothers are also graduate in different disciplines. They all are living in their own village is spite of being highly educated. They could easily move to cities to do attractive official jobs. But city life and official jobs -don’t attract them. They think that they are the sons of the soil and they have an unavoidable obligation to this soil. They not only stuck to their own roots, they have been examples for others to be respectful to their soil.  Mr. Mainul Islam is certainly a person of great (a) ⎯⎯. Being highly educated, he feels no (b) ⎯⎯ to be an ideal farmer. Rather, he takes pride in his (c) ⎯⎯. We all should take lesson from Mr. Mainul. If we follow the (d) ⎯⎯ of Mr. Mainul, our agriculture will develop on one side and job-hunting will be less on the other side. (e) ⎯⎯ of rushing to cities for jobs, we should try to be self-employed at our village. Read the following text carefully and answer the question no. 4 and 5 : Topic : Begum Rokeya  Begum Rokeya was born in 1880, at Pairabond a village in the district in Rangpur. Her family was very conservative. Yet she received her education in English and Bengali from her elder brother Ibrahim Saber. In 1896, at the age of sixteen Rokeya was married to Shakhawat Hossain. Shakhawat was pleased to see the eagerness of his wife for education. In 1909, her husband Shakhawat Hossain died. That same year she opened Shakhawat Memorial Girls' School at Bhagalpur with only five students. But she was forced to close the school in 1910. She reopened the school in 1911 in Calcutta with only 8 female students. In 1917, Lady Chamsford, wife of the then Viceroy of India, visited the school. The school still stands at the heart of the city of Calcutta. In 1916 Begum Rokeya established the Muslim Mahila Samity. Begum Rokeya was a writer also. Through her pen she tried to awaken the Muslim women of the Indian subcontinent. In 1932, on the 9th December, Begum Rokeya died at the age of 52.
